findingsRaw.title: Owner salary above market cost of replacement GM
findingsRaw.reasoning: Dale Brandt drew $160,000 salary (G74, 26 payroll runs) as President, and he is retiring. The buyer will hire a general manager. Replacing him at market reduces cost by the excess plus employer FICA on that excess.
findingsRaw.assumption: Market GM salary of $110,000 for a ~$1.84M-revenue Duluth landscape/snow business. Excess $50,000 plus 7.65% employer FICA = $53,825. Benefits assumed comparable.
findingsRaw.evidence: Dale's W-2s for 3 years, his job description and hours, regional GM salary surveys, and any bonus or distribution history.
findingsRaw.question: Which duties do you perform today (sales, estimating, crew supervision), and would one GM hire cover all of them?

findingsRaw.title: Hansen litigation defense and settlement
findingsRaw.reasoning: Lindqvist & Moe billed $14,500 for 'Litigation - Hansen v. Birchline (retaining wall failure)' plus a $38,000 'Settlement payment ... full & final' (G65). The settlement is labeled full and final. A buyer may still argue that warranty or defect claims recur in a retaining-wall business.
findingsRaw.evidence: Settlement agreement, release, legal invoices, history of prior claims and warranty costs for 3-5 years, and insurance claim correspondence.
findingsRaw.question: Have there been other workmanship or warranty claims in the last five years, and why didn't GL insurance cover this one?

findingsRaw.title: ERC refund for Q3 2021
findingsRaw.reasoning: Other Income includes a $46,000 IRS 'Employee Retention Credit refund - Q3 2021' (G91). It is a one-time government credit that relates to a prior year, so it is not part of ongoing earnings.
findingsRaw.evidence: IRS refund notice, Form 941-X, and ERC eligibility documentation, including any clawback or audit exposure.
findingsRaw.question: Who prepared the ERC claim, and is there any IRS inquiry or recapture risk on it?

findingsRaw.title: One-time derecho storm debris contract
findingsRaw.reasoning: The City of Duluth paid $85,000 for 'Storm debris removal - July 2025 derecho event' phases 1 and 2 (G06), against $41,000 of directly matched subcontractor cost from Superior Tree & Crane (G52). This is event-driven work outside the normal design-build mix. The adjustment removes the $44,000 net margin.
findingsRaw.assumption: Only the matched subcontractor cost is removed. Internal crew labor and fuel used on the job are not quantified, so the true margin may be lower.
findingsRaw.evidence: City contract and purchase orders, job costing for the storm work, and history of any emergency or municipal work in prior years.
findingsRaw.question: Has Birchline done storm-response work for the City in prior years, and how many internal crew hours went into this job?

findingsRaw.title: Jake Brandt paid below market as crew lead
findingsRaw.reasoning: Jake Brandt, likely a family member, is coded as Crew Lead at an implied $12.00/hr over 1,360 hours (G45). The other crew leads earn $23.50-$24.00/hr (G37, G38), and even laborers earn $18.00/hr. A new owner would have to pay market rate to retain or replace him.
findingsRaw.assumption: Market crew-lead rate of $23.50/hr (Ana Reyes, G38) × 1,360 hours = $15,640 incremental wages, plus 7.65% employer FICA = $16,837.
findingsRaw.evidence: Jake's payroll records, timesheets, role description, and family relationship disclosure.
findingsRaw.question: How is Jake related to you, does he truly function as a crew lead, and will he stay after the sale at market pay?

findingsRaw.evidence: SFM policy WC-55821 declarations, payment history, premium audit results, and any accrued liability.
findingsRaw.question: Was the workers' comp policy paid for July-December, cancelled, or moved to another carrier?

findingsRaw.title: Karen Brandt office salary (related party)
findingsRaw.reasoning: Karen Brandt, likely Dale's spouse, is paid $52,000 in Office Salaries (G70), more than the Office Manager, Linda Ortiz, at $48,500 (G71). If her role is real it should be normalized to market. If it is not a working role, the full $52,000 plus taxes is an add-back.
findingsRaw.assumption: Market cost of replacing her office role is $45,000. ($52,000 - $45,000) × 1.0765 FICA = $7,536. If she performs no ongoing role, the add-back would be ~$55,978.
findingsRaw.evidence: Karen's job description, timesheets, and duties, plus confirmation of whether she leaves at closing.
findingsRaw.question: What does Karen do day to day, and will that work need to be replaced after she leaves?

findingsRaw.title: Shop and yard rent paid to Brandt Properties LLC
findingsRaw.reasoning: Rent of $102,000 ($8,500/month) for 4410 Industrial Pkwy is paid to Brandt Properties LLC (G76), an owner-controlled entity. A related-party lease may be above or below market and must be reset to a market lease at closing. The amount is left at zero until a market rent survey is done.
findingsRaw.assumption: No market rent data provided. The adjustment is pending an appraisal or broker opinion, and its direction is unknown.
findingsRaw.evidence: Lease agreement, property square footage and yard acreage, broker opinion of market rent, and the proposed post-closing lease terms.
findingsRaw.question: Will Brandt Properties sign a new multi-year lease with the buyer, and at what rent?

summary: Reported EBITDA of $205,754 is distorted in both directions. There are about $199K of add-backs (excess owner pay, litigation settlement, prepaid 2026 insurance, and personal expenses such as tuition, the Lexus, Maui travel, and club dues) offset by about $135K of deductions (ERC refund, one-off derecho revenue, equipment gain, below-market family labor, and missing workers' comp). That nets to roughly $270K adjusted EBITDA before the unresolved related-party rent and Karen Brandt questions. Earnings quality is moderate: the core maintenance and snow contracts look recurring, but heavy owner-family involvement and loose expense coding mean the buyer should expect diligence push-back and verify every add-back.
